lang.explanation: "Lang" means "long", in distance or in time. The form "langt" can also mean "far": "Det er langt væk" (It is far away).

sentence.da: Giraffen har en **lang** hals.
sentence.en: The giraffe has a long neck.

langfredag.explanation: "Langfredag" means "Good Friday", the Friday before Easter. It is a day off in Denmark, and the name literally means "long Friday".

sentence.da: På **langfredag** har de fleste fri fra arbejde.
sentence.en: On Good Friday most people have the day off work.

langs.explanation: "Langs" means "along" for moving or lying next to a road, a shore or another line you follow: "Vi går langs stranden" (We walk along the beach). Danes can also put it last: "Vi går stranden langs" (We walk along the beach).

sentence.da: Der står træer **langs** vejen.
sentence.en: There are trees along the road.

langsom.explanation: "Langsom" means "slow". To say that something happens slowly, use "langsomt" (slowly): "Tal langsomt, tak" (Speak slowly, please).

sentence.da: Skildpadden er meget **langsom**.
sentence.en: The turtle is very slow.

langt fra.explanation: "Langt fra" means "far from". Say the place right after it: "Hun bor langt fra byen" (She lives far from the town). "Langt væk" (far away) ends the phrase instead: "Hotellet er langt væk" (The hotel is far away). As a full reply, "Langt fra!" means "Far from it!".

forms.en: The hotel is far from the town.

sentence.da: Vores hus ligger **langt fra** byen.
sentence.en: Our house is far from the town.

langt væk.explanation: "Langt væk" means "far away" and ends the phrase: "Hotellet er langt væk" (The hotel is far away). With "langt fra" (far from), say the place after it: "Hun bor langt fra byen" (She lives far from the town).

sentence.da: Min familie bor **langt væk**.
sentence.en: My family lives far away.

langtrukken.explanation: "Langtrukken" means "long-winded", for a speech, story or meeting that goes on longer than people want. It also means drawn out in time or sound: "en langtrukken tone" (a drawn-out tone).

sentence.da: Talen var **langtrukken**, og mange begyndte at gabe.
sentence.en: The speech was long-winded and many began to yawn.

langvarig.explanation: "Langvarig" means "long-lasting". It is about how long something lasts, not how strong it is. "Langvarigt regn" means rain that keeps on, while "kraftigt regn" means heavy rain.

sentence.da: Efter en **langvarig** sygdom kom han endelig tilbage på arbejde.
sentence.en: After a long illness he finally came back to work.

larm.explanation: "Larm" means "noise", the loud, unwanted kind that bothers people. For steady background noise such as traffic and machines, Danes usually say "støj" (noise).

sentence.da: Der er for meget **larm** på gaden.
sentence.en: There is too much noise on the street.

larmende.explanation: "Larmende" means "noisy", for people or places that make an annoying amount of sound. It comes from "at larme" (to make a racket).

sentence.da: Børnene i klassen er **larmende**, når læreren går ud.
sentence.en: The children in the class are noisy when the teacher leaves.

latin.explanation: "Latin" means "Latin", the language of the ancient Romans. Nobody speaks it at home today, but many Danish words in science and medicine come from it.

sentence.da: Lægerne bruger mange ord fra **latin**.
sentence.en: Doctors use many words from Latin.

latterlig.explanation: "Latterlig" means "ridiculous", for something so silly or unreasonable that it is almost funny or annoying.

sentence.da: Det er en **latterlig** pris for en kop kaffe.
sentence.en: That is a ridiculous price for a cup of coffee.

lav.explanation: "Lav" means "low", for something near the ground or small in amount. It works for prices too: "lave priser" (low prices).

sentence.da: Stolen er **lav**, ikke høj.
sentence.en: The chair is low, not high.

lava.explanation: "En lava" means "lava", the hot melted rock that flows out of a volcano. When it cools, it turns into hard stone.

sentence.da: Den røde **lava** flyder ned ad bjergets side.
sentence.en: The red lava flows down the side of the mountain.

ledig.explanation: "Ledig" means "vacant" or "available" and fits a seat, a room, a job or free time. A job that nobody holds is "en ledig stilling" (a job opening), and "Han er ledig" can also mean "He has no job".

sentence.da: Er der en **ledig** plads her?
sentence.en: Is there a free seat here?

legetøj.explanation: "Legetøj" means "toys". This word has no article, so leave out "et": "Jeg har legetøj" (I have toys). When you talk about one specific kind of toy, use its name: "en bamse" (a teddy bear).

sentence.da: Barnet leger med sit **legetøj**.
sentence.en: The child plays with their toys.

leggings.explanation: "Leggings" means "leggings", the stretchy, tight-fitting clothing for the legs. It is always plural, so one pair is "et par leggings" (a pair of leggings).

sentence.da: Hun løber i sorte **leggings** hver morgen.
sentence.en: She runs in black leggings every morning.

lejlighedsvis.explanation: "Lejlighedsvis" means "occasionally", when the chance comes up, without a fixed day or plan. The word comes from "en lejlighed" (an occasion). You say it about something you do now and then: "Jeg spiller lejlighedsvis fodbold" (I play soccer occasionally).

forms.en: He occasionally works as an interpreter

sentence.da: Jeg cykler **lejlighedsvis** på arbejde, når vejret er godt.
sentence.en: I occasionally bike to work when the weather is good.

lektier.explanation: "Lektier" means "homework". It goes with "at lave" (to do): "Jeg laver lektier" (I do my homework). To ask about it, say "Har du lektier for?" (Do you have homework?).

sentence.da: Læreren giver os **lektier** til i morgen.
sentence.en: The teacher gives us homework for tomorrow.

ler.explanation: "Ler" means "clay", the heavy, sticky earth that is soft when wet and gets hard when it dries or is baked hot. Do not mix it up with "ler" in "Han ler" (He laughs), which comes from "at le" (to laugh).

sentence.da: Man former skåle og krukker af vådt **ler**.
sentence.en: You shape bowls and jars from wet clay.

lesbisk.explanation: "Lesbisk" means "lesbian", for women who are attracted to women and for relationships between them: "et lesbisk par" (a lesbian couple).

sentence.da: Hun bor sammen med sin kæreste, og de er et **lesbisk** par.
sentence.en: She lives with her partner, and they are a lesbian couple.

let.explanation: "Let" means "easy" or "light in weight": "en let opgave" (an easy task) and "en let taske" (a light bag). You can tell from the context of the sentence whether it means "easy" or "light in weight".

sentence.da: En fjer er meget **let**.
sentence.en: A feather is very light.

letmælk.explanation: "Letmælk" means "low-fat milk", the everyday milk with 1.5% fat. It is built from let (light) and mælk (milk).

sentence.da: **Letmælk** har mindre fedt end sødmælk.
sentence.en: Low-fat milk has less fat than whole milk.

lettelse.explanation: "Lettelse" means "relief", the good feeling when something that bothered you is over. Someone who feels it is "lettet" (relieved).

sentence.da: Jeg sukkede af **lettelse**, fordi prøven var slut.
sentence.en: I sighed with relief because the test was over.

lettere.explanation: "Lettere" means "easier" and "lighter". It comes from "let" (easy, light).

sentence.da: Min nye taske er **lettere** end den gamle.
sentence.en: My new bag is lighter than the old one.

lettet.explanation: "Lettet" means "relieved", how you feel when a worry goes away. To name the event you are relieved about, use "over" (about): "lettet over, at eksamen var overstået" (relieved that the exam was over).

sentence.da: Jeg var **lettet**, da hun ringede.
sentence.en: I was relieved when she called.

levedygtig.explanation: "Levedygtig" means "viable", able to survive and keep going without help, such as a business, an idea or a baby born too early.

sentence.da: Butikken er **levedygtig**, fordi den tjener flere penge, end den bruger.
sentence.en: The store is viable because it earns more money than it spends.

levende.explanation: "Levende" means "alive" or "living". For music it means "live": "levende musik" (live music).

sentence.da: Kaninen ligger stille, men den er **levende**.
sentence.en: The rabbit lies still, but it is alive.

leverpostej.explanation: "Leverpostej" means "liver pâté", a soft spread for bread. It is made from lever (liver) and postej (pâté). It is usually eaten cold on bread, but it can also be served warm: "lun leverpostej med bacon" (warm liver pâté with bacon).

sentence.da: Til frokost spiser jeg **leverpostej** på rugbrød.
sentence.en: For lunch I eat liver pâté on rye bread.

liberal.explanation: "Liberal" means "liberal". It can mean relaxed and open to the choices of others: "en liberal opdragelse" (a relaxed upbringing). In politics, "et liberalt parti" (a liberal party) wants personal freedom and a small state. It does not mean left-wing as it can in American English.

sentence.da: Han er **liberal** og vil give folk mere frihed og mindre skat.
sentence.en: He is liberal and wants to give people more freedom and less tax.

lidenskab.explanation: "En lidenskab" means "a passion", a very strong feeling of excitement and devotion for a person, a hobby or a cause. The matching describing word is "lidenskabelig" (passionate).

sentence.da: Hans **lidenskab** er musik, og han spiller hver dag.
sentence.en: His passion is music, and he plays every day.

lidenskabelig.explanation: "Lidenskabelig" means "passionate", for a person who feels something very strongly and shows it, and for strong feelings such as love or anger.

sentence.da: Hun bliver **lidenskabelig**, når hun taler om musik.
sentence.en: She becomes passionate when she talks about music.

lidt.explanation: "Lidt" means "a little" or "a bit": "lidt mælk" (a little milk), "lidt træt" (a bit tired). Do not mix it up with "lille" (small): "en lille kop" (a small cup) is about size, while "lidt vand" (a little water) is about amount.

sentence.da: Jeg vil kun have **lidt** mad.
sentence.en: I only want a little food.

lidt efter lidt.explanation: "Lidt efter lidt" means "little by little" and describes change that happens a bit at a time. Word for word, it is "a little after a little".

forms.da: lidt efter lidt bliver det bedre
forms.en: little by little it gets better

sentence.da: **Lidt efter lidt** blev det lyst.
sentence.en: Little by little it got light.

lidt langsommere, tak.explanation: "Lidt langsommere, tak" means "a bit slower, please". "Langsommere" means "slower" (from "langsom", slow). If you also missed the words, add "Kan du sige det igen?" (Can you say that again?).

forms.en: Can you speak a bit slower?

sentence.da: Du taler for hurtigt. **Lidt langsommere, tak**!
sentence.en: You speak too fast. A bit slower, please!

lige.explanation: "Lige" means "straight" or "equal". In "et lige tal" (an even number) it means "even": 2, 4, 6. It is also used for "just" or "right": "lige nu" (right now), "lige ved siden af" (right next to).

sentence.da: Stregen er meget **lige**.
sentence.en: The line is very straight.

lige meget hvad.explanation: "Lige meget hvad" means "no matter what", whatever happens. You say it when you promise something: "Jeg hjælper dig, lige meget hvad" (I will help you, no matter what).

forms.en: I am coming no matter what.

forms.da: Lige meget hvad der sker, ringer jeg.
forms.en: No matter what happens, I will call.

sentence.da: Jeg kommer, **lige meget hvad** der sker.
sentence.en: I will come, no matter what happens.

lige nu.explanation: "Lige nu" means "right now". It is built from lige (just) and nu (now). For something later, use "om lidt" (in a little while).

forms.en: What are you doing right now?

sentence.da: Jeg har ikke tid **lige nu**.
sentence.en: I do not have time right now.

lige om lidt.explanation: "Lige om lidt" means "in just a moment". It is "om lidt" (in a little while) with "lige" (just) added, which promises that something happens very soon.

forms.en: I am coming in just a moment.
We are leaving in just a moment.

sentence.da: Maden er klar **lige om lidt**.
sentence.en: The food will be ready in just a moment.

ligefrem.explanation: "Ligefrem" means "downright", to stress how strong something is: "Det er ligefrem fantastisk" (It is downright fantastic). It can also mean "straightforward" for a person who says things directly: "en ligefrem mand" (a straightforward man).

sentence.da: Det er **ligefrem** utroligt, at han vandt uden at træne.
sentence.en: It is downright unbelievable that he won without training.

ligeglad.explanation: "Ligeglad" means "indifferent" and describes someone who does not care: "Jeg er ligeglad" (I do not mind). Said about a person it can sound rude: "Han er ligeglad med andre" (He does not care about others).

sentence.da: Jeg er **ligeglad**, om vi spiser pizza eller pasta.
sentence.en: I do not mind whether we eat pizza or pasta.

ligegyldig.explanation: "Ligegyldig" means "indifferent" or "unimportant". For a person, it means not caring: "Hun virker ligegyldig" (She seems indifferent). For a thing, it does not matter: "Det er ligegyldigt" (It makes no difference).

sentence.da: Han var **ligegyldig** og hørte ikke efter.
sentence.en: He was indifferent and did not listen.

ligeledes.explanation: "Ligeledes" means "likewise", and says that the same also applies to someone else. As a reply, it answers a wish or greeting: "Rart at møde dig! Ligeledes!" (Nice to meet you! Likewise!)

forms.da: Han kommer, og det gør hun ligeledes
forms.en: He is coming, and so is she

sentence.da: Børn skal have tid til at lege, og voksne **ligeledes**.
sentence.en: Children need time to play, and so do adults.

ligesom.explanation: "Ligesom" means "just like". It is built from lige (just) and som (like). "Lige" also stands alone and adds the sense of "exactly" or "right": "lige nu" (right now), "lige ved siden af" (right next to), "lige meget" (it does not matter).

forms.en: He is just like his father.

sentence.da: Du er **ligesom** din far.
sentence.en: You are just like your father.

ligestilling.explanation: "Ligestilling" means "equality", the idea that everyone gets the same rights and chances, especially in work and pay.

sentence.da: **Ligestilling** betyder, at mænd og kvinder har de samme muligheder.
sentence.en: Equality means that men and women have the same opportunities.

ligeså.explanation: "Ligeså" means "just as", used to say two things are equal: "ligeså høj som dig" (just as tall as you). It can also be written as two words, "lige så", with the same meaning.

sentence.da: Min bror er **ligeså** høj som far, men meget tyndere.
sentence.en: My brother is just as tall as Dad, but much thinner.

ligeud.explanation: "Ligeud" means "straight ahead", used in directions for going on without turning. The turns are "til højre" (to the right) and "til venstre" (to the left).

sentence.da: Ved krydset skal du ikke dreje, men gå **ligeud**.
sentence.en: At the intersection, do not turn, but go straight ahead.

ligeværdig.explanation: "Ligeværdig" means "equal", having equal worth or standing: "en ligeværdig partner" (an equal partner). It does not say they are identical, only that neither counts for more.

sentence.da: I et godt forhold skal man føle sig **ligeværdig**.
sentence.en: In a good relationship you must feel equal.

lignende.explanation: "Lignende" means "similar" and comes before the word it describes: "et lignende problem" (a similar problem). To say one thing looks like another, use "ligner" (looks like): "Han ligner sin far" (He looks like his father).

sentence.da: Jeg har haft et **lignende** problem før.
sentence.en: I have had a similar problem before.

lilla.explanation: "Lilla" means "purple", the color you get from mixing red and blue.

sentence.da: Druer kan være grønne eller **lilla**.
sentence.en: Grapes can be green or purple.

lille.explanation: "Lille" means "small" or "little". It is often a warm word for someone you love: "min lille ven" (my little friend).

sentence.da: Musen er meget **lille**.
sentence.en: The mouse is very small.

lim.explanation: "Lim" means "glue", a sticky liquid that makes two things stick together: "Har du lim til papir?" (Do you have glue for paper?)

sentence.da: **Lim** holder to stykker papir sammen.
sentence.en: Glue holds two pieces of paper together.

linser.explanation: "Linser" means "lentils", small round seeds cooked in soups and stews. One lentil is "en linse", which also means a lens, as in "en kontaktlinse" (a contact lens).

sentence.da: Jeg laver suppe af røde **linser** og gulerødder.
sentence.en: I make soup from red lentils and carrots.

litteratur.explanation: "En litteratur" means "literature", writing that is valued as art, and also all that has been written about a subject: "litteraturen om søvn" (the literature on sleep).

sentence.da: **Litteratur** er for eksempel romaner, digte og skuespil.
sentence.en: Literature is, for example, novels, poems and plays.

livlig.explanation: "Livlig" means "lively", full of movement and noise, for a street, a child or a talk: "en livlig fest" (a lively party). Do not mix it up with "levende" (alive): "et levende dyr" (a living animal).

sentence.da: Gaden er **livlig** om aftenen, fordi mange restauranter har åbent.
sentence.en: The street is lively in the evening because many restaurants are open.

livsglæde.explanation: "En livsglæde" means "joy of life", a strong, happy feeling about being alive that shows in everything a person does.

sentence.da: Selv som gammel mand havde han en stor **livsglæde**.
sentence.en: Even as an old man he had a great zest for life.

livskvalitet.explanation: "Livskvalitet" means "quality of life", how good everyday life feels, including free time and freedom. It is often used about illness and old age: "livskvalitet som ældre" (quality of life as an older person).

sentence.da: Fritid giver mig **livskvalitet**, fordi jeg kan være sammen med familien.
sentence.en: Free time gives me quality of life because I can be with my family.

logik.explanation: "En logik" means "logic", clear step-by-step thinking where each step follows from the one before. It also means the reasoning behind something: "Der er en logik i det" (There is logic in it).

sentence.da: Matematik bygger på **logik**, og hvert trin følger af det forrige.
sentence.en: Math is built on logic, and each step follows from the previous one.

logisk.explanation: "Logisk" means "logical" and is for something that makes sense step by step.

sentence.da: Det er **logisk**, fordi to plus to er fire.
sentence.en: It is logical, because two plus two is four.

lokal.explanation: "Lokal" means "local", for things from the nearby area. "Lokale nyheder" (local news) is news about your own area.

sentence.da: Jeg køber mad hos en **lokal** bager.
sentence.en: I buy food from a local baker.

lokalt.explanation: "Lokalt" means "locally", in your own area rather than far away. Use it with a verb to describe an activity you do close to home: "Jeg handler lokalt" (I shop locally).

sentence.da: Vi handler **lokalt**, fordi vi vil støtte byens bønder.
sentence.en: We shop locally because we want to support the town's farmers.

lommepenge.explanation: "Lommepenge" means "pocket money", money children get to spend. It is built from en lomme (a pocket) and penge (money), and "lomme" also builds "en lommelygte" (a flashlight).

sentence.da: Min datter får hundrede kroner i **lommepenge**.
sentence.en: My daughter gets a hundred kroner in pocket money.

lotto.explanation: "Lotto" means "lotto", a game where you pick numbers and hope they match the draw.

sentence.da: Han håber at vinde i **lotto** i weekenden.
sentence.en: He hopes to win at lotto this weekend.

lovende.explanation: "Lovende" means "promising", for a person or a result that looks likely to succeed. It comes from "at love" (to promise), because the signs seem to promise good things.

sentence.da: De første resultater af forsøget ser **lovende** ud.
sentence.en: The first results of the experiment look promising.

lovgivning.explanation: "Lovgivning" means "legislation", the laws of a country, and also the work of making them. This word has no article, so leave out "en": "Dansk lovgivning gælder for alle" (Danish legislation applies to everyone).

sentence.da: Ny **lovgivning** skal sikre, at alle børn kan komme i skole.
sentence.en: New legislation must ensure that all children can go to school.

lovlig.explanation: "Lovlig" means "legal", allowed by the law. Its opposite is "ulovlig" (illegal).

sentence.da: Det er en **lovlig** handling, fordi loven tillader det.
sentence.en: It is a legal act, because the law allows it.

lovpligtig.explanation: "Lovpligtig" means "mandatory by law", for something the law demands you have or do, not just something sensible. If you ignore the rule, you can be fined.

sentence.da: Alle bilister skal have en forsikring, fordi den er **lovpligtig**.
sentence.en: All drivers must have insurance because it is required by law.

loyal.explanation: "Loyal" means "loyal", staying on someone's side even when it is hard: "en loyal ven" (a loyal friend), "loyale kunder" (loyal customers).

sentence.da: Han var **loyal** over for firmaet, selv da andre sagde op.
sentence.en: He was loyal to the company, even when others quit.

loyalitet.explanation: "Loyalitet" means "loyalty", the feeling of standing by a person, a group or a company.

sentence.da: **Loyalitet** er, at man støtter sine venner, også når det er svært.
sentence.en: Loyalty is when you support your friends, even when it is hard.

luft.explanation: "Luft" means "air". "I luften" means "in the air". It is also the first part of "en lufthavn" (an airport), literally "an air harbor".

sentence.da: Vi åbner vinduet for frisk **luft**.
sentence.en: We open the window for fresh air.

lukket.explanation: "Lukket" means "closed", for doors, shops, windows and roads.

sentence.da: Døren er **lukket**, men vinduet er åbent.
sentence.en: The door is closed, but the window is open.

luksus.explanation: "Luksus" means "luxury", something very comfortable that you do not really need: "Et langt bad er luksus" (A long bath is a luxury).

sentence.da: Det er **luksus** at sove længe i weekenden.
sentence.en: It is a luxury to sleep in on the weekend.

lummer.explanation: "Lummer" means "muggy", for warm, still and damp air, typical before a thunderstorm. It is a heavy feeling in the air, not just heat; for plain heat, use "varm" (warm).

sentence.da: Luften er **lummer**, og der kommer nok tordenvejr snart.
sentence.en: The air is muggy, and a thunderstorm is probably coming soon.

lun.explanation: "Lun" means "warm" or "cozy", pleasantly warm but not hot, for food, rooms and weather: "lun suppe" (warm soup). For humor, it means gentle and dry: "en lun bemærkning" (a gentle remark).

sentence.da: Stuen er **lun**, fordi brændeovnen har brændt hele dagen.
sentence.en: The room is cozy because the wood stove has burned all day.

ly.explanation: "Et ly" means "a shelter", a place that protects you from rain, wind or danger. The phrase "i ly af mørket" (under cover of darkness) means being hidden by something.

related.en: a spot out of the wind

sentence.da: Vi løb ind under et træ for at finde **ly** for regnen.
sentence.en: We ran under a tree to find shelter from the rain.

lydig.explanation: "Lydig" means "obedient", doing what you are told, often said of children and dogs.

sentence.da: Hunden er **lydig** og sætter sig, når jeg siger det.
sentence.en: The dog is obedient and sits down when I say so.

lydløs.explanation: "Lydløs" means "silent", with no noise at all. It is also used for a phone on silent mode: "Min telefon er på lydløs" (My phone is on silent). The ending "-løs" means "without", as in "hjælpeløs" (helpless). For a person who says nothing, use "tavs" (silent): "en tavs mand" (a silent man).

sentence.da: Elbilen er næsten **lydløs**, når den kører langsomt.
sentence.en: The electric car is almost silent when it drives slowly.

lykke.explanation: "Lykke" means "happiness" and also "luck": "Penge giver ikke lykke" (Money does not bring happiness).

sentence.da: Jeg ønsker dig al **lykke** i dit nye hjem.
sentence.en: I wish you all happiness in your new home.

lykkelig.explanation: "Lykkelig" means "happy", in a deeper and longer-lasting way than "glad" (happy in the moment): "Jeg er lykkelig med mit liv" (I am happy with my life). For a good mood today, "glad" is more common: "Jeg er glad i dag" (I am happy today).

sentence.da: Hun er **lykkelig** med sit nye job.
sentence.en: She is happy with her new job.

lyn.explanation: "Et lyn" means "lightning", or "a flash of lightning". "Hurtig som et lyn" means "fast as lightning".

sentence.da: Man ser **lyn** først og hører torden bagefter.
sentence.en: You see lightning first and hear thunder afterward.

lyng.explanation: "En lyng" means "heather", a low plant with tiny purple flowers that covers open, sandy land.

sentence.da: På heden vokser der **lyng**, og den blomstrer lilla.
sentence.en: On the heath there grows heather, and it blooms purple.

lys.explanation: "Lys" means "light" (not dark) or "bright", for light colors and for rooms or days full of daylight. There is also a different word "et lys", which means "a candle" or "a light": "Tænd et lys" (Light a candle).

sentence.da: Stuen er meget **lys** i dag.
sentence.en: The living room is very bright today.

lyseblå.explanation: "Lyseblå" means "light blue". Putting "lyse-" (light) in front of a color makes it lighter, and "mørke-" (dark) makes it darker.

sentence.da: Himlen er **lyseblå** i dag.
sentence.en: The sky is light blue today.

lysegrøn.explanation: "Lysegrøn" means "light green". Putting "lyse-" (light) in front of a color makes it lighter, and "mørke-" (dark) makes it darker.

sentence.da: Salaten er **lysegrøn**.
sentence.en: The lettuce is light green.

lysende.explanation: "Lysende" means "bright" or "luminous", for something that shines by itself. With colors it means very strong: "lysende gul" (bright yellow).

sentence.da: Fyrtårnet er **lysende** og viser skibene vej i mørket.
sentence.en: The lighthouse is bright and shows the ships the way in the dark.

lyserød.explanation: "Lyserød" means "pink". It is lys (light) and rød (red), so it is literally light red, but Danish uses it only for pink.

sentence.da: Grisen er **lyserød**.
sentence.en: The pig is pink.

lyshåret.explanation: "Lyshåret" means "fair-haired", for a person whose hair is pale or golden. It is built from lys (light) and hår (hair).

sentence.da: Hendes bror er **lyshåret**, men hun selv har mørkt hår.
sentence.en: Her brother is fair-haired, but she herself has dark hair.

læder.explanation: "Læder" means "leather". For fake leather, say "kunstlæder" (faux leather).

sentence.da: **Læder** laves af huden fra en ko.
sentence.en: Leather is made from the skin of a cow.

lækker.explanation: "Lækker" means "delicious" or "tasty", and also "great-looking": "en lækker bil" (a great-looking car).

sentence.da: Kagen er meget **lækker**.
sentence.en: The cake is really delicious.

længe.explanation: "Længe" means "for a long time", for time: "Hvor længe bliver du?" (How long are you staying?) "For længe siden" means "a long time ago". Do not mix it up with "lang" (long), which describes a thing: "en lang vej" (a long road).

sentence.da: Jeg har ventet **længe** på bussen.
sentence.en: I have waited a long time for the bus.

længst.explanation: "Længst" means "longest" for distance and time: "Hvem har boet her længst?" (Who has lived here the longest?) It also fits "furthest": "Hvem bor længst væk?" (Who lives the furthest away?)

sentence.da: Min bror bor **længst** fra os.
sentence.en: My brother lives the furthest from us.

læseforståelse.explanation: "En læseforståelse" means "reading comprehension", how well you grasp what you have read. A child can read every word aloud and still miss what it means. It is built from at læse (to read) and en forståelse (an understanding).

sentence.da: Ved en test i **læseforståelse** svarer eleverne på spørgsmål om en tekst.
sentence.en: In a test of reading comprehension, the students answer questions about a text.

løbende.explanation: "Løbende" means "continuously", as something goes on over time, not just once: "Vi opdaterer siden løbende" (We update the page on an ongoing basis). It comes from "at løbe" (to run): "løbende vand" (running water) and "løbende udgifter" (ongoing costs).

sentence.da: Vi tjekker priserne **løbende**, fordi de ændrer sig hver uge.
sentence.en: We check the prices continuously because they change every week.

lørdag.explanation: "En lørdag" means "a Saturday". "På lørdag" means "on Saturday" (the coming one), and "om lørdagen" means "on Saturdays" (every Saturday). Day names start with a lowercase letter in Danish.

sentence.da: Vi har fri på **lørdag**.
sentence.en: We are off on Saturday.

løs.explanation: "Løs" means "loose", not held in place: "Hunden er løs" (The dog is loose).

sentence.da: Min tand er **løs**, og den falder snart ud.
sentence.en: My tooth is loose, and it will fall out soon.

løvfald.explanation: "Et løvfald" means "leaf fall", the time before winter when trees lose their leaves. "Løv" is the word for the leaves on trees: "Træerne mister løvet" (The trees lose their leaves). For one leaf, say "et blad" (a leaf).

sentence.da: Efter **løvfald** ligger bladene tykt på jorden.
sentence.en: After leaf fall the leaves lie thick on the ground.

at male.explanation: "At male" means "to paint": "Han maler væggen hvid" (He paints the wall white). It is also used for making pictures: "Hun maler et billede" (She paints a picture). For drawing with a pencil, use "at tegne" (to draw).

sentence.da: Vi vil **male** huset gult.
sentence.en: We want to paint the house yellow.

at mangle.explanation: "At mangle" means "to lack" or "to be missing": "Jeg mangler en pen" (I am missing a pen). With "der" (there) at the start: "Der mangler en stol" (A chair is missing).

sentence.da: Børn må ikke **mangle** mad og tøj.
sentence.en: Children must not lack food and clothes.

at manipulere.explanation: "At manipulere" means "to manipulate", to influence someone or something in a hidden or unfair way. For numbers or records, it means to change them on purpose: "at manipulere tal" (to manipulate numbers).

sentence.da: Reklamer kan **manipulere** børn til at ønske sig legetøj.
sentence.en: Ads can manipulate children into wanting toys.

at markere.explanation: "At markere" means "to mark", to make something stand out so you can find it again, such as a line on paper or text on a screen. For an event, it means to celebrate it: "at markere en fødselsdag" (to mark a birthday).

sentence.da: Du skal **markere** det vigtigste med en gul tusch.
sentence.en: You must mark the most important part with a yellow marker.
